patients.label: Original COPD rehabilitation case
attribution_limitations: Selective improvement: narrative and abstract report improvement in 6MWD, CAT and the SGRQ symptom domain, but Table 2 Phase 2 SGRQ total rose 55->56, impact 34->39 and activity stayed 80. Do not generalize to all health-status domains.

Cross-phase comparability: Phase 1 and Phase 2 start from different states (intervening readmission/stabilization) and authors acknowledge baseline differences in disease severity and timing relative to hospitalization. Do not infer treatment effect or causation (including the authors' "synergistic" claim) from the two phases.
Adherence: the abstract says improved adherence, but formal adherence and usability assessments were not conducted; no numeric adherence measure exists. Figure 3 plots exercise minutes only.

Telerehabilitation equipment and monitoring are described for "patients" (plural) although this is a single case; individual provision/use of each device and the frequency/duration of tele-sessions are not stated.

Admission vs Phase 1 baseline nutrition values differ without stated timing (GNRI 86.1 at admission in text vs 88 at Phase 1 baseline in Table 2). Table 2 does not state when Phase 1 baseline was measured relative to discharge; do not equate them.

Table 1 CRP unit is printed as mg/L (value 0.03, reference <0.3) while the table note converts only creatinine units; the printed unit is retained, not corrected. Several results sit at or near printed reference limits (Hb, Ht, RBC, creatinine at lower limit; eGFR 93.4 vs 50-93; total protein 63.1 vs 64.3-78.4) and no diagnosis or flag is inferred from the comparison.

The index admission is described as the "second lifetime episode" of AECOPD; the week-8 readmission episode also met GOLD AECOPD criteria, but its ordinal and the interval from the prior admission are not stated. Inpatient treatment of the readmission is not itemized.
Table 2 dashes (CSQ-8 and AECOPD diagnosis at Baseline/Delta) denote not assessed/not applicable and are not negative findings. Delta columns are source-printed changes, not separate encounters.

External literature must not be assigned to the patient: Hansen et al. 10-week telerehabilitation study (17.2 m 6MWD, 1.7-point CAT), cited MCID thresholds and telemonitoring reports are other studies.

Not documented: named corticosteroid/bronchodilator/antibiotic agents or doses, smoking history, comorbidities other than COPD/underweight, tele-session frequency, and follow-up beyond the eight-week combined program.

claims.text: A 72-year-old man with severe GOLD IV COPD, mMRC grade 3 dyspnea and long-term oxygen had limited indoor activity, although he drove to weekly outpatient visits. Pre-admission FEV1 was 0.60 L (28.8% predicted), FEV1/FVC 33.7%, VC 1.79 L (57.4% predicted) and FVC 1.78 L (57.1% predicted). He was admitted for his second lifetime AECOPD after dyspnea at rest, with barrel chest, diminished breath sounds, Hoover sign and accessory-muscle hypertrophy, hyperinflated lungs, and reported compensated respiratory acidosis under 2 L/min nasal oxygen (pH 7.31/PaCO2 59.6/PaO2 59/HCO3 29.5). He was underweight (BMI 15.6/GNRI 86.1), with no significant inflammatory, anemia or renal dysfunction by narrative; all admission table values are retained.

claims.text: Inpatient care included corticosteroids, bronchodilators, prophylactic antibiotics, ABG-titrated oxygen, twice-daily pulmonary rehab 5–6 days/week, nutrition/pharmaceutical support and counseling. After discharge he received weekly outpatient conditioning, resistance and 20-minute ergometer work at 40% predicted maximum workload targeting Borg 4–5. Dyspnea/exercise intolerance and participation worsened; activity at 2–3 METs produced Borg >5, and wheezing/dyspnea with recurrent AECOPD led to week-eight readmission. Phase 1 6MWD fell 290→220 m, CAT rose 16→19, and SGRQ symptoms 88→95; CSQ-8 was 21 with lower satisfaction on treatment/time-support items.

claims.text: After inpatient stabilization, an eight-week combined outpatient/video rehabilitation program mirrored the outpatient exercises by videoconference and visually confirmed diet/bronchodilator use. Home activity and unsupervised training increased and he consistently attended supervised sessions, with no qualifying AECOPD. Phase 2 6MWD rose 244→276 m, CAT 23→16, SGRQ symptoms 77→67 and CSQ-8 21→26 from Phase 2 baseline to week 8. Other SGRQ domains did not uniformly improve: total 55→56, impact 34→39 and activity unchanged at 80. No adverse events/dropouts were reported, but formal adherence/usability were not assessed and anxiety/depression were not fully evaluated. Follow-up was limited to the intervention; causal prevention or longer-term benefit is not established.
